title: CGO: calling C from Go and what you give up by doing so

videos.script: Go can call C. You write C in a comment directly above one import line, and the go command hands it to gcc. This lesson is about that bridge, and about the bill that comes with it. {{preamble}} It starts small. A C function written in the comment, a function from the maths library, and the types that keep the two languages apart. Then you watch the build run gcc five times for seven lines of C. {{memory}} Next, a real C library: zlib, the code behind gzip. Every call hands memory across the line. Some of it you must free yourself. Some of it C must never keep. Break one of those rules and the runtime panics, and you will see it do so. {{cost}} Then the price of a single call. A call into C costs more than thirty Go calls. And a C function that blocks holds a whole thread while it waits. {{binary}} Then what the program gives up. It needs shared libraries to start. It no longer cross-compiles. One C dependency adds half a minute to a cold build. And a crash in C takes every goroutine down with it. {{choice}} So the lesson ends with a decision. When is C worth all that, and what should you look for first?
